messages.author: c5b4a1199682ea80
messages.subject: Randomly assigned/sampled categorical covariates
parts:
Trying to fit a regression model in which the categories of the covariate or only known as proportions (ie for each value out of N, the covariate level is ‘1’ with probability p.clim1 and ‘2’ with  probability 1 – p.clim1) using the categorical() distribution in rstan.

(somewhat more applied: exploring biological records from different countries involves some uncertainty about the associated climate zones, as some countries are located within several  different climate zones).

 

Tried various options but none works so far…..Thanks for any help!

 

 

 

This is my Stan code

#-------------------------------------------------------------------------

cat(

  " 

data {

            int<lower=0> N;        

            int<lower=0> C;

            int<lower=0, upper=1> Obs[N];        

            matrix[N,C] propClimZone;

}

parameters {

            real mu;

            real<lower=0, upper=1> pi1; 

            vector[C] beta;

}

model {

            int<lower=1> clim[N];

            for(n in 1:N)

                        clim[n]~categorical(propClimZone[n]);

            for(n in 1:N)

                        Obs[n] ~ bernoulli_logit(mu +beta * clim[n]);

            beta ~ normal(0, 10);

}

"

, file="model.stan")

#-------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

 

This data-generating R code

#--------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

set.seed(1)

N = 20

Obs = rbinom(N, 1, 0.4)

p.clim1 <- round(runif(N, 0,1), 2)

propClimZone <- matrix(NA, ncol=2, nrow=N)

propClimZone[,1] <-  p.clim1

propClimZone[,2] <-  1- p.clim1

C=2

 

dat2stan = list(N = N, C = C, Obs = Obs, propClimZone = propClimZone)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Randomly assigned/sampled categorical covariates
parts:
If you can write out your models data and parameter variable
shapes and sizes and write down the density, we can help you code
in Stan. It's hard to guess what you're trying to do from code
that doesn't work.

For instance, here's what I'd want for a simple regression:

data: y an N-vector of scalar observations
x an N-vector of predictors

parameters: alpha scalar slope
beta scalar intercept
sigma noise scale (must be positive)

density: p(y, alpha, beta, sigma | x) =
normal(y | x * alpha + beta, sigma)
* normal(alpha | 0, 1)
* normal(beta | 0, 1)
* cauchy(sigma | 0, 2)

Once you have that, translating to Stan is easy.

- Bob

messages.author: c5b4a1199682ea80
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Randomly assigned/sampled categorical covariates
parts:
Here's what a logistic regression model with two latent variables (uncertainty in the covariates) may look like. For each data point yn in N there are two latent variables z1n in {1,…C} and z2n in {1…R} with categorical distributions parameterized by the two matrices Q1 and Q2.  Q1 and Q2 are matrices, as the mixing proportions may vary for each data point. I included two latent covariates, as start towards a multiple regression problem.   


 data:  y  an N-vector of binary observations
        Theta1  an N×C matrix of mixing proportions  (where theta1(n,c) ≥0 and rowsums = 1)

        Theta2  an N×R matrix of mixing proportions (where theta2(n,c) ≥0 and rowsums = 1)


 parameters: mu   scalar intercept
                     alpha1  vector of coefficients for each level in C

                     alpha2  vector of coefficients for each level in R

transformed parameters:

                        z1 latent variable in {1,…C}

                        z2 latent variable in {1,…R}


 density:  p(y | Theta1, Theta2, mu, alpha1, alpha2) =
                 Bernoulli(y | mu + alpha1[z1[n]] + alpha2[z2[n]] )
                 * categorical(z1 | Theta1)

                 * categorical(z2 | Theta2)
                 * normal(alpha1 | 0,  1)

                 * normal(alpha2 | 0,  1)
                 * normal(mu | 0,  1)

 

Mixture models seem to be the way to go but so far I have problems, some linked to use matrices of mixing proportions

 

Thanks for all help. Learning Stan is fun!

Konstans

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Randomly assigned/sampled categorical covariates
parts:
The density you're defining is the joint over the latent
parameters

p(y, Theta, mu, alpha, z)

not the data sampling distribution,

p(y | Theta, mu, alpha)

And you need a product over the n in the Bernoulli, but now
I see what you're doing.

The big issue is that Stan doesn't support discrete parameters!
So you can define the model this way, but you can't code it this
way in Stan. You have to treat it as a mixture model, as Andrew
saw right away. This will work and actually be much more efficient
than sampling the unknown levels if there aren't too many level
combinations.

You need marginalize the z out as follows:

p(y, Theta, mu, alpha)

= p(Theta, mu, alpha) // priors

* PROD_{n in 1:N} p(y[n] | Theta, mu, alpha)

The key is this step:

p(y[n] | Theta, mu, alpha)

= SUM_z[n] p(z[n]) p(y[n] | z[n], mu, alpha)

And it's a double sum, because z is 2D; and you need to use
log_sum_exp as explained in the chapter on mixtures and on
marginalizing out discrete parameters.

There'll still be a label switching non-identifiability (as
explained in the problematic posteriors chapter of the manual),
but that's to be expected with a 2D latent structure.

- Bob
